summary: Michael J. Sweet specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa and later served there as a clinical assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry (attested 1996, 2006).
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned a Master of Arts at San Diego State University under the supervision of Sandra A. Wawrytko, attested in 2011.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a B.Soc.Sc. from the University of Cape Town and an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara, where he later pursued doctoral studies under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist. He earned his PhD from the University of Vienna and completed his Habilitation at the University of Zurich, holding posts at Zurich (1995) and the University of Münster (2002).

Michael Jansen was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at RWTH Aachen University, Bonn, Rome, and Delhi. He served as architecture dean at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999), founding rector of GUtech (2007–2008), and president of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from UC Santa Barbara under Mark Juergensmeyer. He held faculty posts at Eckerd College (~2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (~2012–2021).
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter worked in Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Larry William Moses, was a research fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (2000), and served as an editorial consultant and cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington.
Michael M. Broido worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.

Michael Oppitz is a scholar of Tibetology and related fields. He held an appointment at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as a director (Leiter) at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).
Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He was appointed Associate Professor (~1995) and later Walter C. Klein Professor of Chinese History and Anthropology (~2013) at Harvard.

Michael Pye is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds, he held posts at Leeds (~1974–1978), Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster (1991–1994), and Otani University (~2004–2007).

Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at Harvard University. He held positions at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.
Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held dictionary and staff positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1979, 1992, 2008) and worked with the KOHD project and University of Göttingen.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).
Michael Silverstein was a linguist who was educated at Harvard University (~1962–1971). He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from around 1970 until 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker specializes in Sinology and religious studies, earning an MA at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2006). He held posts at Nanyang Technological University, University of Leipzig, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, and University of Pittsburgh.

Michael Torsten Much is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He was a visiting Alexander von Humboldt Foundation fellow at the University of Hamburg.
